citations.anchor: refuses a row written by another provider, naming both
citations.why: A read of a row whose storage_provider differs from the configured provider.id is refused instead of streamed — the read-path comparison the invariant names.

citations.anchor: skips an asset written by a different provider
citations.why: The blob-reclaim path (deletion and purge) asserts the provider.id comparison: a foreign row's key is never handed to the configured backend.

citations.anchor: rejects a provider with no id — the value every asset row records
citations.why: Assembly refuses a provider without an id, which is what makes 'written into every row' possible at all.

citations.anchor: refuses to boot over assets written by another provider, naming it and the count
citations.why: onApplicationBootstrap rejects and the message is matched against the foreign id and the row count — exactly the abort the invariant describes.

citations.anchor: skips the check when media_asset is not queryable yet
citations.why: A missing-relation error resolves rather than rejects — the 'a missing table is not a refusal' half.

citations.anchor: rejects a declared directUrl capability with no directUrl()
citations.why: MediaServerPlugin() throws when capabilities.directUrl is true without an implementation — the first of the two assembly-time checks.

citations.anchor: refuses signed-url serving on a backend that cannot sign
citations.why: MediaServerPlugin() throws for directServe: 'signed-url' on a provider declaring directUrl: false, and the sibling case accepts it on one that can.

citations.anchor: leaves nothing behind when the body errors mid-stream
citations.why: The put rejects and the storage root is asserted empty — no partial blob and no key handed out.

citations.anchor: describeStorageProvider('media-provider-local'
citations.why: Runs the shared contract's 'is all-or-nothing when the body fails mid-stream' case with a real storedKeys() probe, so a surviving blob fails the suite.

citations.anchor: rejects for a missing key instead of failing mid-stream
citations.why: get() rejects with ObjectNotFoundError before any stream is opened for a key that was never written.

citations.anchor: is idempotent — a missing key is a no-op
citations.why: remove() on an already-removed key and on a never-written key both resolve — the idempotence clause.

citations.anchor: rejects rather than throwing synchronously from every method
citations.why: put/get/remove are each called with a poisoned argument and the return value is asserted to be a Promise, so a synchronous throw fails the test.

citations.anchor: keys a derivative under the reserved variants/ namespace, so it cannot collide with an original of the same name
citations.why: A PutObject with isVariant lands under variants/ and the same-named original is asserted intact.

citations.anchor: describeStorageProvider('media-provider-local'
citations.why: Runs the shared contract's 'keeps a derivative clear of an original with the same name' case, which every adapter's spec also runs.

citations.anchor: serves the original when the requested variant does not exist
citations.why: Uploads bytes Sharp cannot decode: the upload still returns 201 and the row carries variants [] with null dimensions — best-effort derivatives that never fail the upload.

citations.anchor: removes the original and every derivative
citations.why: reclaimAssetBlobs walks Asset.storageKeys, so a derivative left behind fails. The 'a rolled-back deletion destroys no bytes' half is not pinned anywhere.

citations.anchor: holds the bytes after an upload and drops them on delete
citations.why: Asserts the blob store is empty after DELETE /media/assets — the bytes, not just the row, are freed.

citations.anchor: streams to a member of the owning workspace, ignoring the header
citations.why: The raw route serves an asset whose workspace is not the one in X-Workspace-Id, proving the scope comes from the asset's row rather than the header.

citations.anchor: 404s for a user who is not a member of the owning workspace
citations.why: A viewer holding media:read but no membership gets a 404 — the membership requirement on the one guard-free route. The 'every other route carries WorkspaceGuard' half is not pinned.

citations.anchor: answers 404 when the blob is missing from disk
citations.why: Row kept, bytes deleted: the response is the same 404 a missing id gets, not a 500 or a truncated 200.

citations.anchor: does not name the storage key in the 404 body
citations.why: Asserts the body carries neither the asset id nor the words 'storage key' — the second clause verbatim.

citations.anchor: still 404s an asset that does not exist
citations.why: The non-existent-id arm of the same-404 set, alongside the non-member arm pinned in media-assets.spec.

citations.anchor: refuses to serve a file outside the storage root when the stored key traverses
citations.why: A storage_key rewritten to ../ gives status 500 (asserted explicitly, and contrasted with the missing-blob 404) and the outside file's contents never reach the body.

citations.anchor: always sends nosniff and a no-capability CSP
citations.why: Asserts X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff plus a CSP containing default-src 'none' and sandbox on every download.

citations.anchor: serves a scripted SVG as an attachment too
citations.why: SVG is served as an attachment over the real route — the 'SVG is not on the inline allowlist' clause.

citations.anchor: hardens the token-authenticated /v1 download the same way
citations.why: Pins that the second raw route (the token half) carries the same nosniff + CSP, which is what 'both raw routes' means.

citations.anchor: authorizes before it redirects — a non-member gets the same 404
citations.why: A non-member gets 404 rather than a 302, so the redirect cannot precede the authorization check.

citations.anchor: never caches the redirect, which outlives the URL it points at
citations.why: Asserts Cache-Control: private, no-store on the 302.

citations.anchor: redirects an image to a signed URL instead of streaming it
citations.why: The signed URL carries disposition and type as query parameters; the sibling .html case asserts the disposition flips to attachment — the 'pinned type and disposition' clause.

citations.anchor: accepts a file of exactly the cap
citations.why: A body of exactly maxUploadBytes returns 201 — the inclusive half, which busboy's >= limit used to break.

citations.anchor: rejects one byte over the cap with a 413 that names the limit
citations.why: cap + 1 is a 413 carrying MulterUploadFilter's message rather than 'File too large'.

citations.anchor: applies the same cap to the token upload route
citations.why: The configured cap (1024) also bounds POST /api/v1/media/assets, so a route with its own FileInterceptor limit would not honour it.

citations.anchor: describe('FileName', () => {
citations.why: The whole suite: empty, whitespace-only, over 255, a forward slash, a backslash, NUL, LF, CR and DEL each throw InvalidFileNameError, and a plain name is only trimmed — rejected, not cleaned.

citations.anchor: falls back to the original for a bogus ?variant=
citations.why: ?variant=toString and ?variant=constructor both serve the original PNG at 200 — a bare index would have returned a truthy prototype member and handed the provider an undefined key.

citations.anchor: serves the original when the requested variant does not exist
citations.why: ?variant=thumb on an asset with no derivatives is a 200 of the original, not an error.

citations.anchor: rejects a non-uuid folderId with 400, not 500
citations.why: Pins that an unparseable folderId is rejected by the query rather than reaching the driver.

citations.anchor: rejects an unknown kind with 400, not 500
citations.why: Pins the second half of the same clause for ?kind=.

citations.anchor: treats % and _ in ?search= as literal characters
citations.why: A search for % or _ matches only names/tags containing that character, rather than acting as a LIKE wildcard.

citations.anchor: does not count a blank alt as covered
citations.why: An alt of '' and an alt of '   ' both count as missing — the 'a space is never counted as coverage' half. The 'normalised identically on every write path' half is not pinned: the rows are seeded directly, bypassing upload and PATCH.

citations.anchor: never lets any token curate the media library
citations.why: Asserts media:update and media:delete are absent from both the read and full scope permission sets — the invariant's second clause verbatim.

citations.anchor: lets a read-only token fetch bytes but never upload
citations.why: A read token gets 200 on /raw and 403 on the upload route — the 'can only upload (full) and read bytes (both)' half, end to end.

citations.anchor: 404s when the header names another workspace in the same bucket
citations.why: A two-workspace token asking for an asset from the workspace it did not name gets 404, so X-Workspace-Id is binding rather than advisory.

citations.anchor: 404s an asset outside the request
citations.why: The same claim over the public-API suite: an asset uploaded under one workspace of the bucket 404s when the header names the other.

citations.anchor: shows the shared tools to a read-scoped token
citations.why: tools/list over MCP contains media_assets_search, media_folders_list and media_asset_read — the three reading tools on the MCP surface.

citations.anchor: offers every read tool in the catalogue to an admin
citations.why: The same three tools appear in the copilot's offer — the other half of 'visible to both surfaces'.

citations.anchor: shows no copilot-only tool, whatever the scope
citations.why: media_propose_alt_text and media_propose_file are asserted absent from tools/list at any token scope — the 'proposals to the copilot only' clause.

citations.anchor: gives an MCP caller the bearer-fetchable download path
citations.why: The search result's downloadPath is /api/v1/... on the MCP surface, and is fetched with the bearer to prove it is presentation of the same asset.

citations.anchor: carries a download path the asking user
citations.why: The same field is /api/media/... on the copilot surface, which is what makes downloadPath the surface-dependent one.

citations.anchor: describe('isReadableMimeType', () => {
citations.why: The allowlist itself: text types pass, PDF/octet-stream/etc. are refused, parameters stripped and case ignored.

citations.anchor: cuts a file longer than the cap short and says so
citations.why: The byte ceiling is applied while reading (the sibling case asserts the stream stops being pulled) and the result is marked truncated.

citations.anchor: refuses bytes that are not valid UTF-8
citations.why: A decoding failure is fatal rather than yielding replacement characters.

citations.anchor: drops an incomplete trailing codepoint instead of throwing
citations.why: The one exception the invariant carves out: a multi-byte character cut by the cap is dropped, not reported as invalid.

citations.anchor: rejects a path and names the parameter that does the job
citations.why: A name containing a slash is a tool error naming folderId, end to end. The 1 MB ceiling and 'the applier calls the same UploadAssetUseCase' are not pinned.

citations.anchor: rejects a format outside the enum
citations.why: A format outside FILE_FORMAT_NAMES is refused — the closed-enumeration clause.

citations.anchor: names the folder parameter in the path message
citations.why: The unit-level pin of the same path rejection: resolveFileName refuses a name with a separator and the message names folderId.

citations.anchor: removes media and token-bucket rows that no foreign key reaches
citations.why: media_asset and media_folder counts go from non-zero to zero on DELETE /api/workspaces/:id. The 'frees their blobs' and 'no per-item domain events' clauses are not pinned by any test.

citations.anchor: says the library failed to load, not that it is empty
citations.why: A failed media read renders an error state with a Retry and the empty-state wording is asserted hidden. The 'no media:read starts no queries at all' half is not pinned — media-library.spec asserts the no-access card, not the absence of requests.

citations.anchor: stages an upload and sends it only when the record is saved
citations.why: The upload spy stays at 0 until Save, then goes to 1 and the saved value holds the real id. The 'a failed upload aborts the whole save' and 'no second upload on retry' clauses are not pinned.
